chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Hamadhānī, who said:

I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding a man who begins with Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm in his salat only in Umm al-Kitāb, then when he proceeds to other than Umm al-Kitāb from the surah, he leaves it? Al-ʿAyyāshī said: There is no harm in that.
So he wrote in his own hand: He must repeat it twice, despite his objection — meaning al-ʿAyyāshī.

key_terms.أُمِّ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, the Opening Chapter of the Qur'an.
key_terms.السُّورَةِ: The additional surah recited after al-Fātiḥah in salat.
key_terms.الْعَيَّاشِيُّ: The person whose opinion is being rejected in this report.
key_terms.بِبِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ: The basmalah recited in salat before a surah.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on omitting بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ before the second surah in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on reciting Bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm in salat when moving from Sūrat al-Fātiḥah to another surah. The Imam عليه السلام rejects the view that omitting it is unobjectionable and instructs that it be repeated, emphasizing the legal importance of the basmalah in recitation.
